gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they cover (1) module-level AUB sweep with auto-selection, (2) system-candidate sweep, then (3) an automatically-generated “next fix” suggestion report based on the latest results.

## 1) Module autopilot (select best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for afterward:
- A newly selected/bumped “best” module candidate (or a note that nothing beats `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`).
- Any regressions on `tuning_min` and `lockbox_min` (mins matter given your current floor is strong on lockbox: ~3.318).

## 2) System autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to look for:
- Whether any system candidate improves **both** mean and min versus current champion, or at least improves mean without violating a min-floor you care about.
- Any candidates that improve tuning while harming lockbox (or vice versa). Given current stats, lockbox is already relatively strong; you may decide to prioritize tuning mean/min uplift.

## 3) Generate next-fix report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
Then open:
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`

This should propose targeted follow-ups based on failure patterns / near-miss candidates.

## Quick sanity checks before/after running
- Ensure the referenced champion file exists: `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`.
- Capture stdout/stderr logs (or redirect to a run log) so you can diff decisions made by `--select-best`.
- Confirm no “INCONCLUSIVE” items are pending (handoff shows none), so you can safely promote a winner if one appears.

If you paste the outputs/summaries from (1) and (2), I can help decide whether to promote a new champion or adjust selection criteria (e.g., guardrails on `min` metrics).
